title: Galois group and degree bound for a finite multiradical extension
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in $F$, and suppose $X^n-1$ splits over $F$. Let $r\geq0$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in F^\times$. In an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], choose $\alpha_j$ with $\alpha_j^n=a_j$ and set $L=F(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)$. Then $L/F$ is a finite Galois extension (finite-dimensional, normal and separable). Put $\mu_n(F)=\{z\in F^\times:z^n=1\}$. The map
$$\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)\longrightarrow\mu_n(F)^r,\qquad\sigma\longmapsto(\sigma(\alpha_j)/\alpha_j)_{j=1}^r$$
is an injective homomorphism of groups, and $[L:F]\mid n^r$. Field extensions and their finite degrees use [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-vector-space-dimension]; normal means that every irreducible polynomial over $F$ with a root in $L$ splits there; separability uses [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. No binomial $X^n-a_j$ is assumed irreducible. For $r=0$, $L=F$ and the target group is the trivial group.

source.place: Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph: injective Kummer character and cyclic degree dividing n for one root; the displayed finite-list formulation is its product-character version.

proof.text: If $r=0$, $L=F$; its $F$-automorphism group and the empty product are trivial. Their unique map is injective, and $[F:F]=1\mid n^0=1$. Assume $r>0$.

source.place: Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph, finite-list product-character version; assembly of the extracted inputs.

proof.text: Apply the binomial root-torsor lemma to each $a_j$ and to $1$. It gives separability of $X^n-a_j$, nonzero $\alpha_j$, $|\mu_n(F)|=n$, and all roots of these binomials as $\alpha_j\zeta$. In the algebraic extension $\Omega/F$, let $S$ be its separable subfield. Its root description puts every $\alpha_j$ in $S$, so $L\subseteq S$. Every $x\in L$ is separable over $F$: the evaluation kernels of $F[X]\to L$ and $F[X]\to S$ at $x$ coincide under the injective inclusion, hence so do their monic generators, the minimal polynomials.

source.place: Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph, finite-list product-character version; assembly of the extracted inputs.

proof.text: The root-torsor factorization gives $X^n-a_j=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_n(F)}(X-\alpha_j\zeta)$ in $L[X]$, by injectivity of $L[X]\to\Omega[X]$. Thus $P=\prod_j(X^n-a_j)$ splits over $L$ and has positive degree $rn$. All its roots are in $L$, and each $\alpha_j$ is a root (take $\zeta=1$), so its roots generate exactly $L$. The finite-normal splitting-field theorem gives finite dimensionality and normality. Together with the preceding separability this makes $L/F$ finite Galois. Repeated generators do not require $P$ to be separable.

source.place: Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph, finite-list product-character version; assembly of the extracted inputs.

proof.text: For every $F$-automorphism $\sigma$ of $L$, $(\sigma(\alpha_j)/\alpha_j)^n=\sigma(a_j)/a_j=1$. The root-torsor lemma with $a=1$ therefore places this ratio in the image of the finite scalar group $U=\mu_n(F)$. Apply the generated-field scalar-character lemma with $E=L$ and $b_j=\alpha_j$. Its hypotheses hold because these nonzero elements generate $L$. It gives the injective homomorphism with precisely the displayed ratio coordinates, and $|\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)|\mid|U|^r=n^r$.

source.place: Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph, finite-list product-character version; assembly of the extracted inputs.

proof.text: The finite-Galois order theorem applies to $L/F$ and gives $|\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)|=[L:F]$. Substituting in the preceding divisibility yields $[L:F]\mid n^r$.
